chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who has upon him a camel as an obligation for ransom, he said: 'If he cannot find a camel, then seven sheep. And if he is not able, he should fast for eighteen days.'

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A young female camel, used here as the primary unit of expiation
key_terms.فِدَاءٌ: Ransom or expiation offered to compensate for a religious obligation or transgression

ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy of expiation for killing a wild animal while in Ihram if one cannot afford a camel?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the graduated financial and devotional penalties (kaffarah) for killing game while in Ihram, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease (taysir) when resources are limited. It establishes a clear hierarchy: starting with a camel, then seven sheep, and finally eighteen days of fasting, ensuring the expiation remains accessible regardless of the individual's economic status.
